title: EU AI Act Article 50(1): Transparency for Direct Interaction -- What AI Operators Must Disclose From 2 August 2026
context: 2026-08-28 -- Article 50 transparency obligations are live; operators of conversational and assistant AI must disclose machine interaction by default
body: From 2 August 2026, Article 50(1) of the EU AI Act requires every AI system intended to interact directly with natural persons to be designed so that the person is informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless that is obvious from the circumstances and the context of use. For chatbots, voice assistants, and copilots, the safe default is explicit disclosure at the point of first interaction. Article 50(2) adds a second, harder obligation for generative outputs: synthetic audio, image, video, and text content must be marked in a machine-readable format and detectably labelled as artificially generated. The Council of AI treats the two obligations as one transparency surface: a conversational system that is honestly labelled as AI still needs its generative outputs to carry machine-readable provenance so downstream systems can tell human-authored from machine-generated material. Its verified measurement credential records, for each system, whether direct-interaction disclosure and machine-readable marking are both present -- a pass/fail that is independently signed rather than self-attested. Practical steps for operators before the enforcement window tightens: (1) audit every customer-facing assistant for an explicit AI disclosure string; (2) add machine-readable output marking to generative endpoints; (3) retain a signed measurement run showing both controls active, so a regulator's transparency question is answered with evidence, not a claim.
